first.rationale: The competitor's aggressive entry pricing is actively pulling price-sensitive SMB accounts, making promotional_pricing the most directly responsive lever this week, and memory_73 suggests it previously drove both acquisition and revenue lift while also improving time-to-value. However, the primary objective is sustainable long-term qualified revenue, and discount-driven acquisition carries real risk of attracting low-quality or price-only-motivated accounts that churn once promotions end or margins erode — this tension isn't resolved by the memory as summarized, so I want to verify the original record to check whether the lift was durable/qualified revenue or just short-term volume. I also want to verify memory_31 (signup simplification) since activation and onboarding are independently down this quarter and a low-risk structural fix might be a safer or complementary path if promotional pricing's long-term revenue quality is uncertain. Given only one experiment slot and competing plausible causes for the SMB erosion (price competition vs. structural onboarding/activation decay), I'm committing to promotional_pricing but scoping it as a small guarded test rather than a broad rollout, since the inherited memory doesn't verify long-run retention/quality of the acquired revenue and a full rollout could lock in a value-eroding pattern before that's known.
